---
title: "Mallard Duck Movement"
---

Mallards (*Anas platyrhynchos*) tagged at Lake Constance—a large freshwater lake along the border of southern Germany, Switzerland, and Austria—spend much of their time near home waters, but several migrate hundreds of kilometers northeast across Germany, Czechia, and Poland toward breeding grounds in northeastern Europe. Across the year, the ducks spend most hours resting or dabbling locally at speeds well under 1 m/s, with movement speeds and longer flights picking up noticeably in late summer and early autumn (July–October) and again during spring migration (February–April).

This project analyzes more than 83,000 GPS tracking fixes from 52 individual mallards collected between 2007 and 2017 by researchers at Radolfzell and published through the Movebank animal-tracking repository. Use the navigation bar above to explore the [Map](map.qmd) page, which plots the birds' geographic tracks across Central and Eastern Europe, and the [Seasons](seasons.qmd) page, which compares monthly movement-speed distributions throughout the calendar year.
